title: EMC English Conversation Club
description:
**EMC English Conversation Club**
**Thursdays, 4 to 6pm**
**Free.** Please **join this group** and **reserve** your seat every week.

Whether you want to improve your English or you're a native speaker keen to help others, this is a great place to connect and build friendships.

Please **join this group** and **reserve** your seat every week.

title: Who Are We Building For? Product and Sales on ICP and UVP
description:
Sales says Product isn't building what customers need. Product says Sales is promising features that don't exist. Both may be right, and both may be missing the real problem: they're trying to understand the customer separately.

In this session, Ren will draw on 30 years in tech sales to show why your Ideal Customer Profile (ICP) and Unique Value Proposition (UVP) work best when Product and Sales develop them together. Strategy should start with the market opportunity and the client, not with product ideation or features.

This won't be a one-way talk. Ren will share real stories and use cases from enterprise deals, including how shared customer evidence turned a single client request into a roadmap priority. We'll also run a hands-on workshop on UVP frameworks, so you can practise turning "here's what our product does" into "here's your situation and what changes."

You'll walk away with:

\- A clearer view of who Product and Sales should each define in an ICP\, and where they should work together
\- A way to tell a one\-off feature request from a real market signal
\- Turn product features into a buyer\-focused UVP

Who it's for: Product managers and product leaders, and anyone who works closely with Sales or customers.

Huge thanks to Auror for hosting and sponsoring this event!

You can join the livestream here: [https://meet.google.com/npk-dmyt-ddj](https://meet.google.com/npk-dmyt-ddj). As always the livestream will kick off from just before 6pm.

Note that our host venue has asked that we send you the exact location of the event on the day a couple of hours before the start time - the venue is in the Britomart area. Those of you who have attended events at Auror before will know where it is!

title: JuniorDev Auckland Meet
location: 125 The Strand, Parnell, Auckland 1010, New Zealand, Auckland
description:
We’re happy to announce the next **JuniorDev Auckland event**!

Join us for an evening of learning and connection as we hear from our speakers and the experiences they’ll be sharing.

**Important Note for Attendees:**

* **Please note of the new location for the event: [Directions to Serko House](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1M8Jt_-5DmBABSiNnaDpCpNiHNfxMRCICI1eRBjne-08/edit?tab=t.0) (Just 2 mins away from Xero)**

**Talk 1: Finding Joy After AI: An Inside Out Look at How We Work by Kevin Meneses**
Inspired by Disney and Pixar's Inside Out films, this (pre-recorded) talk uses their premise as a framework to explore what team survey data reveals about AI adoption, productivity, and working hours, offering practical ways to thrive in an AI-assisted workflow.

**A bit about Kevin:**

* Kevin is a Junior Software Engineer at Fergus who transitioned into engineering from the Customer Support team after completing a full stack developer programme.

**Talk 2: Building AI without Losing Our Values by**
**Lauren Peate**
AI is here to stay – hype, copyright theft, data worker mistreatment, environmental harm, and all. If you care about people and the planet but also need to understand new tech, what can you do? I’ll recommend a middle ground – using AI in features and workflows without compromising our values. Combining my own experience with insights from our original research with hundreds of global developers, I’ll share examples of how to use this tech with care.

**A bit about Lauren:**

* Lauren Peate is a data nerd who cares about people. She’s founder and CEO of Multitudes, which turns engineering metrics into a tool for continuous improvement – in AI, engineering productivity, developer experience, and more. Through her career, she’s worked with a wide range of organizations, from Fortune 500 tech companies in San Francisco to startups in the Middle East. Previously on a PhD track, she started her career conducting independent research through a Fulbright grant.

title: Arrival
location: 2 Freyberg Place, Auckland CBD, Auckland 1000, New Zealand, Auckland
description:
Over the years that we have been showing films at the EMC, we have let our Sci-Fi members down somewhat. And I confess - I am not into Sci Fi. Too many space ships and odd looking aliens I thought

Well, sic-fi can be immensely satisfying and thought provoking. Now we start to make up for avoiding such films! Alien space ships land around the globe and an expert linguist is hired to work out whether the aliens have come in peace or not.

The film was nominated for best picture, best performance by the lead actress and best original score for a film (I don't remember showing a film nominated for this award)

The Telegraph (UK) reviewer wrote: "introspective, philosophical and existentially inclined—yet [it] unfolds in an unwavering tenor of chest-tightening excitement. And there is a mid-film revelation—less a sudden twist than sleek unwinding of everything you think you know—that feels, when it hits you, like your seat is tipping back.

Definitely worth the look!
